finding_key: packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts::a table cell that is not an object is silently skipped rather than repaired or rejected, leaving a stored shape the table renderer dereferences unconditionally.

verdict.reasoning: In the supplied `assertValidElementData` (table arm) the loop does `if (!cell || typeof cell !== 'object' || Array.isArray(cell)) continue;`, so a cell that is a string, number, or array is neither repaired nor rejected — it is stored verbatim, while the very next lines repair an absent `body` for the same reason. The slides table renderer (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts) only guards `if (!cell || isCovered(cell)) continue;` and then dereferences `cell.style.fill` in `paintCellFills`, `cell.body` in `computeTableLayout`, and `cell.body.blocks` in `paintCellContents`, so a non-object cell is a TypeError for every viewer — exactly the class of shape the diff's own rest-api.md rule says is rejected rather than persisted. (A `null` cell is in fact tolerated by the renderer's `!cell` guard, so the finding overstates that one sub-case.) Impact is bounded: only a hand-written API payload produces such a cell, no editor does, and the same walk has sibling holes (e.g. a non-object `row`), so this reads as one instance of an incomplete-but-defence-in-depth validator rather than a user-facing break.

finding_key: packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts::array / non-object table cells are silently skipped by the new guard and stored, crashing the renderer — inconsistent with the array rejection the same diff adds for a text element's `data`

finding_key: packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts::table-element repair fills in `cell.body` but leaves `cell.style`, `columnwidths` and non-object cells/rows unrepaired — the same stored-crash it claims to close

finding_key: packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts::color-reset test cannot distinguish `{ color: undefined }` from `{}` — the exact distinction the fix depends on

verdict.reasoning: The new test (packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts:82,88) asserts `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })`; Vitest/Jest's `toHaveBeenCalledWith` uses the same recursive equality as `toEqual`, which ignores explicitly-`undefined` own properties, so a call with `{}` would satisfy it equally. This is a test-adequacy weakness, not a production defect, hence minor.

finding_key: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts::the usable oauth url is now printed only when `open()` throws, so a headless/no-browser environment can be left with no way to continue

finding_key: packages/cli/src/bin.ts::production entrypoint uses `program.parse()` (sync) with async action handlers, so the behavior the new `--quiet` guard asserts via `parseasync` is not what ships

finding_key: packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs::adding index.html's own families (inter/fraunces/jetbrains mono) to the font gate makes every visual capture, in every section, hard-depend on fonts.googleapis.com resolving within 10s

verdict.reasoning: The mechanics of the claim check out against the supplied code: `index.html:12` pulls Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono on every harness page load, and `waitForFontsReady()` is invoked from `capturePass()` for every page (harness-root plus each of the five sections, times four profiles), so the new `VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES`/`VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS` check poll at verify-visual-browser.mjs (~line 384, `{timeout: 10000}`) now gates all captures on those remote faces reaching `loaded`, whereas previously only the lazily-injected Korean/Roboto families were polled — families that non-slides pages never register, so `fonts.check()` fell through to system fonts and returned true. The swallowed `.catch(() => {})` on `fonts.load` does convert a fast rejection into a 10s timeout, and because the throw escapes `capturePass` the whole run aborts rather than reporting per-target diffs. Two mitigations temper severity: if fonts.googleapis.com is wholly unreachable the css2 stylesheet fails, no FontFaces are registered, and the poll passes trivially (the claim correctly scopes its failure to the "CSS loads, binaries fail/slow" case), and the baselines already encode Inter glyphs, so a font-less run would fail on pixel diffs anyway — the change mostly broadens/relabels an existing dependency rather than inventing one. I could not verify the CI lane's actual egress, and the withheld task doc is where that risk posture is argued, hence medium confidence.

finding_key: packages/frontend/src/components/theme-provider.tsx::`readstoredtheme` result is cast to `theme` without validation; a junk stored value can throw from `classlist.add`

finding_key: packages/docs/src/model/color.ts::`resolvestoredcolor` only collapses the bare `''` before the resolver, so the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` form the docstring calls reachable lands on the docs default instead of the theme color
